identity.title: POCUS cardiac: pericardial effusion (subxiphoid/PLAX), with RA/RV diastolic collapse for tamponade

technique.how: Phased-array probe: subxiphoid four-chamber (liver as window, probe flat) and parasternal long axis (3rd-4th left ICS). Look for an anechoic stripe between epicardium and bright pericardium, circumferential vs dependent; grade thickness in diastole. For tamponade look for RA collapse in late diastole/early systole, RV free-wall diastolic collapse, swinging heart and plethoric IVC.
technique.prerequisites: Supine or left lateral position; adjust depth to include the posterior pericardium.

interpretation.positive_finding: Any anechoic pericardial stripe = effusion; ED physician detection has sensitivity 0.96 and specificity 0.98 versus cardiology review. Effusion plus RA/RV diastolic collapse and a dilated non-collapsing IVC in a hypotensive patient indicates tamponade physiology.
interpretation.negative_finding: No pericardial fluid on adequate subxiphoid and parasternal windows effectively excludes tamponade as the cause of shock; it does not exclude pericarditis.
interpretation.pitfalls: Epicardial fat pad (anterior, hypoechoic, moves with heart) and left pleural effusion (posterior to descending aorta on PLAX) mimic effusion. Loculated post-surgical or clotted hemopericardium can be missed; tamponade is a clinical diagnosis and chamber collapse can be absent with elevated right-sided pressures.
interpretation.changes_what: Effusion + collapse/plethoric IVC + shock: emergent pericardiocentesis or surgery. Effusion without collapse: formal echo and etiology workup. No effusion: drop tamponade from the shock differential.

estimates.target_condition: Pericardial effusion (presence/absence) on ED bedside echocardiography
estimates.population: 515 ED patients with high-risk criteria for pericardial effusion; 103 with effusion; operators: emergency physicians trained in ultrasonography
estimates.reference_standard: Review of all captured images by the Department of Cardiology
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.96/(1-0.98); LR- = (1-0.96)/0.98 from sensitivity 96%, specificity 98% (Mandavia 2001 abstract); prevalence = 103/515; CIs not computed
estimates.quote: Emergency physicians detected pericardial effusion with a sensitivity of 96% (95% confidence interval [CI] 90.4% to 98.9%), specificity of 98% (95% CI 95.8% to 99.1%)

estimates.target_condition: Pericardial effusion in trauma (eFAST cardiac component)
estimates.population: Trauma patients undergoing eFAST; 75 studies, 24,350 patients (all components); mostly emergency-physician operators
estimates.reference_standard: CT, formal echocardiography, surgery or pericardial window (varies by study)

sources.citation: Mandavia DP, Hoffner RJ, Mahaney K, Henderson SO. Bedside echocardiography by emergency physicians. Ann Emerg Med. 2001;38(4):377-382.
Netherton S, Milenkovic V, Taylor M, Davis PJ. Diagnostic accuracy of eFAST in the trauma patient: a systematic review and meta-analysis. CJEM. 2019;21(6):727-738.
Roy CL, Minor MA, Brookhart MA, Choudhry NK. Does this patient with a pericardial effusion have cardiac tamponade? JAMA. 2007;297(16):1810-1818.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use a single poor-quality window to exclude effusion; do not diagnose tamponade from effusion size alone, and do not rely on absence of chamber collapse when pulmonary hypertension or RV hypertrophy is present.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Effusion with hypotension, tachycardia, pulsus paradoxus >10 mm Hg or RV diastolic collapse: emergent cardiology/cardiothoracic involvement and pericardiocentesis; in penetrating trauma with hemopericardium, thoracotomy pathway.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Mandavia 2001 reference standard was cardiology over-read of the same images (not an independent echo), which may overestimate agreement; eFAST pooled sensitivity 0.91 comes from heterogeneous operators and reference standards.
safety_scope.skill_assumption: Operator trained in focused cardiac ultrasound (subxiphoid and PLAX windows, fat-pad vs effusion, pleural vs pericardial fluid) and in recognizing RA/RV diastolic collapse and IVC plethora; tamponade findings require confirmation by a credentialed echocardiographer when time allows.

extraction_notes: Mandavia 2001 PMID confirmed as 11574793 (anchor listed it as unconfirmed). Effusion-detection sens/spec quoted from abstract; LRs computed. eFAST meta-analysis added as trauma-population estimate. Roy 2007 RCE cited for tamponade clinical context (pulsus paradoxus LR 3.3 / 0.03) but not entered as an estimate because it is not a POCUS finding; POCUS accuracy for RA/RV collapse in diagnosing tamponade was not located as a quotable pooled estimate within budget.
